root.help:
one — workspace development

USAGE
  one <command> [options]

EVERYDAY COMMANDS
  create        Create a workspace
  add           Add a module
  run           List and execute workspace tasks
  exec          Execute a command with module variables
  env           Manage environment variables
  login         Sign in to Infisical locally or over SSH

COMMON OPTIONS
  -o, --output  Output format: json | yaml | text
  -h, --help    Show help
  -v, --version Show version

EXAMPLES
  one create demo
  one add
  one dev
  one build -p web
  one test -p web

All commands: one help --all
Task shorthand: one <task> = one run <task> (built-ins take precedence)
Command help: one <command> --help

auth.login.short: Sign in to Infisical locally or over SSH
auth.login.tip:
Sign in to Infisical. Local sessions open a browser and wait for its callback.

Over SSH, or with --no-browser, open the displayed URL in a browser on your own computer. Complete sign-in, copy the browser's CLI login token, and paste it into the hidden terminal prompt. No SSH port forwarding is needed. Sign-in expires after 10 minutes. Manual sign-in requires an interactive terminal. Credentials are stored in plaintext in ~/.one/config/session.json (or $ONE_HOME/config/session.json), with file mode 0600 on Unix. No system credential store is required.

SSH sessions enable --no-browser automatically. Use --no-browser=false to open a browser on the machine running One.

EXAMPLES
  one login
  one login --no-browser
  one login --no-browser --site-url https://infisical.example.com

Sign in with one login.

Run one env bind to select an existing project or create an Infisical project for the workspace interactively. Use --create to explicitly create and bind storage, or --project-id to bind an existing Secret Manager project. Existing bindings are preserved. Workspace bindings are saved to one.manifest.toml, with default environment dev. Without a binding, set fails instead of creating a project.

Login automatically creates or reuses shared-credentials in the current organization, with dev as the default environment. Run one env bind --global to retry initialization or silently recover a binding from another account; --env changes the default environment. Bindings are stored locally per instance, account and organization. --create is only available for workspace binding and cannot be combined with --global.

Shows the saved language preference and the language active in this terminal. Pass auto, zh-CN, or en-US to change the preference.

auto follows LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, then LANG; the fallback is English. One Desktop shares this preference. Module and third-party tool logs keep their original language.
exec.tip:
Runs a command in the selected module directory. Select a module by name or relative path, or run from inside a module. The positional module and --project must agree when both are used.

Use -- to separate One options from the child command. When the workspace has an env.infisical binding, variables are fetched from Infisical and injected into the child process. --env selects the environment. Injected values override same-name shell variables. Without a binding, the shell environment is used directly. Local .env files are not loaded by One.

With --global, provide --env and --path explicitly. The command keeps the current working directory. Use --keys to select shared credentials.

One does not print injected variable values. Child stdout and stderr pass through unchanged.

Check for the latest stable One CLI release and update the current executable.
Downloads are verified with SHA256 and a version check. An equal or newer

Only official stable release builds can upgrade. On Windows, the verified
update is installed after this command exits.

skills.short: Forward commands to the upstream Skills CLI

Run npx skills@1.8.1 with all arguments unchanged in the current directory.
One prepares Node when it is missing and preserves upstream interaction, output,
and exit codes. Use one skills --help for upstream help.

Official One skills are initially installed from the CLI bundle and registered
with their GitHub master source. Use one skills update --project for later
updates. Legacy local copies can be registered with one init skills; use
--dry-run to preview. Upstream updates may replace local edits.

Business skills are installed only on request from their GitHub repositories.
One does not add --global, --agent, or the Skills CLI --yes flag to manual commands.

skills.init_short: Initialize official One skills and register their update source
skills.init_tip:
Install missing official One skills from this CLI and register their GitHub source
in skills-lock.json. With no --skill, initialize one-cli and inspect other installed
One skills. Use --skill to select specific official skills.

Existing files are never replaced. Unchanged legacy local copies can be registered;
modified files and other sources are preserved. Preview with --dry-run.
After registration, use one skills update --project for updates from the recorded
GitHub branch. Upstream updates may replace local edits.

Use --install-recommend to scan workspace modules and select missing skills.
Choose agents, workspace/global scope and symlink/copy mode once, then review
the installation before starting. The upstream Skills API handles installation
and lock files. Failed targets can be retried without reinstalling successful ones.
--yes skips all prompts; --agent, --global and --copy set installation options.
--dry-run only previews recommendations and does not download anything.
Use -o json for the structured result; progress goes to stderr.
This mode installs official skills from GitHub. Regular initialization uses
bundled files. --skill and --install-recommend cannot be combined.
